title.zh: 卷九 補列傳第一 後宮
title.raw: 卷九 補列傳第一 後宮 Volume 9 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts

sentences.zh: 神武婁后

translations.literal: Empress Lou of Shenwu
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lou of Shenwu

sentences.zh: 神武明皇后婁氏，諱昭君，贈司徒內干之女也。

translations.literal: Empress Ming, Lady Lou, taboo name Zhaojun, was the daughter of Neigan, posthumously appointed Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ming, née Lou, whose personal name was Zhaojun, was the daughter of Neigan, posthumously appointed Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 少明悟，強族多聘之，並不肯行。

translations.literal: From youth she was bright and perceptive; powerful clans sought her in marriage many times, yet she would not go.
translations.idiomatic: From girlhood she was bright and perceptive. Powerful clans sought her hand again and again, yet she would not consent.

sentences.zh: 及見神武於城上執役，驚曰：「此真吾夫也。

translations.literal: When she saw Shenwu performing labor on the city wall, she was startled and said: "This is truly my husband.
translations.idiomatic: When she saw Gao Huan laboring on the city wall, she started and said, "This is truly my husband.

sentences.zh: 」乃使婢通意，又數致私財，使以聘己，父母不得已而許焉。

translations.literal: " She then sent a maid to convey her feelings, and repeatedly sent private funds so that he might betroth her; her parents, having no choice, consented.
translations.idiomatic: " She sent a maid to convey her feelings and repeatedly sent private funds so that he might betroth her; her parents, having no choice, consented.

sentences.zh: 神武既有澄清之志，傾產以結英豪，密謀秘策，后恒參預。

translations.literal: Once Shenwu had the will to restore order, he spent his estate to win over heroes; in secret plots and hidden stratagems the empress always took part.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gao Huan resolved to restore order, he spent his estate to win over heroes; in secret plots and hidden stratagems Empress Lou always took part.

sentences.zh: 及拜渤海王妃，閫闈之事悉決焉。

translations.literal: When he was enfeoffed Princess Consort of Bohai, all affairs of the inner quarters were decided by her.
translations.idiomatic: When he was enfeoffed Princess Consort of Bohai, all affairs of the inner quarters were decided by her.

sentences.zh: 后高明嚴斷，雅遵儉約，往來外舍，侍從不過十人。

translations.literal: The empress was lofty, clear, and stern in judgment; she always observed thrift; when going out to external residences, her attendants never exceeded ten.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was lofty in judgment, clear-minded, and stern; she always observed thrift, and when she went out to external residences her attendants never exceeded ten.

sentences.zh: 性寬厚，不妒忌，神武姬侍，咸加恩待。

translations.literal: Her nature was generous and she was not jealous; Shenwu's concubines and attendants she all treated with favor.
translations.idiomatic: Her nature was generous and free of jealousy; Gao Huan's concubines and attendants she treated with equal favor.

sentences.zh: 神武嘗將西討出師，後夜孿生一男一女，左右以危急，請追告神武。

translations.literal: Once when Shenwu was about to march west on campaign, the empress at night bore twins, a boy and a girl; those beside her, finding the situation perilous, asked to send word after Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Once, as Gao Huan was about to march west on campaign, the empress gave birth at night to twins, a boy and a girl. Those beside her, finding the situation perilous, asked to send word after him.

sentences.zh: 后弗聽曰：「王出統大兵，何得以我故輕離軍幕。

translations.literal: The empress would not listen and said: "The king has gone forth to command a great army — how can he lightly leave the command tent on my account.
translations.idiomatic: The empress would not hear of it. "The king has gone forth to command a great army," she said. "How can he lightly leave the command tent on my account?

sentences.zh: 死生命也，來復何為！

translations.literal: Life and death are fate — what use is it if he comes back!
translations.idiomatic: Life and death are fate — what use is it if he comes back!

sentences.zh: 」神武聞之，嗟歎良久。

translations.literal: " When Shenwu heard of it, he sighed in admiration for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: " When Gao Huan heard of it, he sighed in admiration for a long while.

sentences.zh: 沙苑敗後，侯景屢言請精騎二萬，必能取之。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Shaya, Hou Jing repeatedly asked for twenty thousand picked cavalry, saying he could certainly recover it.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Shaya, Hou Jing repeatedly asked for twenty thousand picked cavalry, saying he could certainly recover the lost ground.

sentences.zh: 神武悅，以告于后。

translations.literal: Shenwu was pleased and told the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was pleased and told the empress.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「若如其言，豈有還理，得獺失景，亦有何利。

translations.literal: The empress said: "If it comes about as he says, could there be any coming back — gain the otter, lose Jing; what profit is there.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "If things go as he promises, do you suppose he would ever return? You would gain some paltry conquest and lose Hou Jing — what profit is there in that?

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he desisted.

sentences.zh: 神武逼於茹茹，欲娶其女而未決。

translations.literal: Shenwu, pressed by the Rouran, wished to marry their princess but had not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan, pressed by the Rouran, wished to marry their princess but had not yet decided.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「國家大計，願不疑也。

translations.literal: The empress said: "This is a great plan for the state — do not hesitate.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "This is a great plan for the state — do not hesitate.

sentences.zh: 」及茹茹公主至，后避正室處之。

translations.literal: " When the Rouran princess arrived, the empress vacated the main chamber to lodge her.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Rouran princess arrived, the empress vacated the main chamber to lodge her.

sentences.zh: 神武愧而拜謝焉，曰：「彼將有覺，願絕勿顧。

translations.literal: Shenwu, ashamed, bowed and apologized to her, saying: "She will notice — please sever all ties and do not look back.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan, ashamed, bowed and apologized to her, saying, "She will notice — please sever all ties and do not look back.

sentences.zh: 」慈愛諸子，不異己出，躬自紡績，人賜一袍一袴。

translations.literal: " She loved all the sons as if they were her own; she personally spun and wove, giving each man one robe and one pair of trousers.
translations.idiomatic: " She loved all the sons as if they were her own; she personally spun and wove, giving each man one robe and one pair of trousers.

sentences.zh: 手縫戎服，以帥左右。

translations.literal: With her own hands she sewed military garments to lead those beside her.
translations.idiomatic: With her own hands she sewed military garments to set an example for those beside her.

sentences.zh: 弟昭，以功名自達，其餘親屬，未嘗為請爵位。

translations.literal: Her younger brother Zhao attained distinction through merit; as for the rest of her kin, she never once asked for noble rank on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger brother Zhao attained distinction through merit; as for the rest of her kin, she never once asked for noble rank on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 每言有材當用，義不以私亂公。

translations.literal: She always said that talent should be employed when found, and that righteousness must not let private feeling disorder public duty.
translations.idiomatic: She always said that talent should be employed when found, and that righteousness must not let private feeling disorder public duty.

sentences.zh: 文襄嗣位，進為太妃。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang succeeded to the throne, she was advanced to Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng succeeded to the throne, she was advanced to Grand Consort.

sentences.zh: 文宣將受魏禪，后固執不許，帝所以中止。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan was about to receive the Wei abdication, the empress firmly refused to permit it, and the emperor therefore desisted.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yang was about to receive the Wei abdication, the empress firmly refused to permit it, and the emperor therefore desisted.

sentences.zh: 天保初，尊為皇太后，宮曰宣訓。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, she was honored as Empress Dowager; her palace was named Xuanxun.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianbao era, she was honored as Empress Dowager; her palace was named Xuanxun.

sentences.zh: 濟南即位，尊為太皇太后。

translations.literal: When the Emperor of Jinan succeeded, she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor of Jinan succeeded, she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 尚書令楊愔等受遺詔輔政，疏忌諸王。

translations.literal: Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing Yang Yin and others received the testamentary edict to assist in government and kept the princes at a distance in suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Yang Yin and others received the testamentary edict to assist in government and kept the princes at a distance in suspicion.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后密與孝昭及諸大將定策誅之，下令廢立。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager secretly joined Xiaozhao and the great generals in fixing a plan to execute them, and issued an edict deposing and enthroning.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager secretly joined Gao Yan and the great generals in fixing a plan to execute them, and issued an edict deposing one ruler and enthroning another.

sentences.zh: 孝昭即位，復為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao succeeded, she again became Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yan succeeded, she again became Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 孝昭帝崩，太后又下詔立武成帝。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao died, the empress dowager again issued an edict enthroning Emperor Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhao died, the empress dowager again issued an edict enthroning Emperor Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 大寧二年春，太后寢疾，衣忽自舉，用巫媼言改姓石氏。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Daning, the empress dowager fell ill; her garments suddenly lifted of themselves, and following a sorceress's words she changed her surname to Shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Daning, the empress dowager fell ill; her garments suddenly lifted of themselves, and following a sorceress's words she changed her surname to Shi.

sentences.zh: 四月辛丑，崩於北宮，時年六十二。

translations.literal: On the xinchou day of the fourth month she died at the Northern Palace, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day of the fourth month she died at the Northern Palace, aged sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 五月甲申，合葬義平陵。

translations.literal: On the jiashen day of the fifth month she was interred with Shenwu at Yiping Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day of the fifth month she was interred with Gao Huan at Yiping Tomb.

sentences.zh: 太后凡孕六男二女，皆感夢：孕文襄則夢一斷龍；

translations.literal: The empress dowager in all bore six sons and two daughters, each pregnancy attended by a dream: when she conceived Wenxiang she dreamed of a severed dragon;
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager in all bore six sons and two daughters, each pregnancy attended by a dream: when she conceived Gao Cheng she dreamed of a severed dragon;

sentences.zh: 孕文宣則夢大龍，首尾屬天地，張口動目，勢狀驚人；

translations.literal: when she conceived Wenxuan she dreamed of a great dragon whose head and tail joined heaven and earth, mouth open and eyes moving, its aspect terrifying;
translations.idiomatic: when she conceived Gao Yang she dreamed of a great dragon whose head and tail joined heaven and earth, mouth open and eyes moving, its aspect terrifying;

sentences.zh: 孕孝昭則夢蠕龍於地；

translations.literal: when she conceived Xiaozhao she dreamed of a writhing dragon upon the ground;
translations.idiomatic: when she conceived Gao Yan she dreamed of a writhing dragon upon the ground;

sentences.zh: 孕武成則夢龍浴於海；

translations.literal: when she conceived Wucheng she dreamed of a dragon bathing in the sea;
translations.idiomatic: when she conceived Gao Zhan she dreamed of a dragon bathing in the sea;

sentences.zh: 孕魏二后並夢月入懷；

translations.literal: when she conceived the two Wei empresses she both dreamed of the moon entering the bosom;
translations.idiomatic: when she conceived the two Wei empresses she both dreamed of the moon entering the bosom;

sentences.zh: 孕襄城、博陵二王夢鼠入衣下。

translations.literal: when she conceived the Princes of Xiangcheng and Boling she dreamed of rats entering beneath the garments.
translations.idiomatic: when she conceived the Princes of Xiangcheng and Boling she dreamed of rats entering beneath the garments.

sentences.zh: 后未崩，有童謠曰「九龍母死不作孝」。

translations.literal: Before the empress dowager died, a children's rhyme said: "Nine dragons — when the mother dies, no mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Before the empress dowager died, a children's rhyme ran: "Nine dragons — when the mother dies, no mourning."

sentences.zh: 及后崩，武成不改服，緋袍如故。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager died, Wucheng did not change his garments and kept his crimson robe as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager died, Wucheng did not change his garments and kept his crimson robe as before.

sentences.zh: 未幾，登三臺，置酒作樂。

translations.literal: Before long he ascended the Three Towers, set out wine, and made music.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he ascended the Three Towers, set out wine, and made music.

sentences.zh: 帝女進白袍，帝怒，投諸臺下。

translations.literal: The emperor's daughter brought a white robe; the emperor was angry and cast it down from the tower.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's daughter brought a white robe; the emperor was angry and cast it down from the tower.

sentences.zh: 和士開請止樂，帝大怒，撻之。

translations.literal: He Shikai asked that the music be stopped; the emperor was greatly angered and beat him.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai asked that the music be stopped; the emperor was greatly angered and beat him.

sentences.zh: 帝於昆季次實九，蓋其徵驗也。

translations.literal: The emperor among his brothers by birth was actually ninth — surely this was the omen's fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor among his brothers by birth was actually ninth — surely this was the omen's fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 文襄元后

translations.literal: Empress Yuan of Wenxiang
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yuan of Wenxiang

sentences.zh: 文襄敬皇后元氏，魏孝靜帝之姊也。

translations.literal: Reverent Empress Yuan of Wenxiang was the elder sister of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Reverent Empress Yuan of Wenxiang was the elder sister of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝時，封馮翊公主而歸於文襄。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei she was enfeoffed Princess of Fengyi and given in marriage to Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei she was enfeoffed Princess of Fengyi and given in marriage to Gao Cheng.

sentences.zh: 容德兼美，曲盡和敬。

translations.literal: Her bearing and virtue were both beautiful; in harmony and reverence she exhausted every measure.
translations.idiomatic: Her bearing and virtue were both beautiful; in harmony and reverence she exhausted every measure.

sentences.zh: 初生河間王孝琬，時文襄為世子，三日而孝靜帝幸世子第，贈錦彩及布帛萬匹。

translations.literal: When she first bore Prince Xiaowan of Hejian, Wenxiang was then heir; on the third day Emperor Xiaojing visited the heir's residence and bestowed brocades, silks, and cloth in ten thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: When she first bore Prince Xiaowan of Hejian, Gao Cheng was then heir; on the third day Emperor Xiaojing visited the heir's residence and bestowed brocades, silks, and cloth in ten thousand bolts.

sentences.zh: 世子辭，求通受諸貴禮遺，於是十屋皆滿。

translations.literal: The heir declined and asked instead to receive the gifts and presents of the nobles; thereupon ten rooms were filled.
translations.idiomatic: The heir declined and asked instead to receive the gifts and presents of the nobles; thereupon ten rooms were filled.

sentences.zh: 次生兩公主。

translations.literal: Next she bore two princesses.
translations.idiomatic: Next she bore two princesses.

sentences.zh: 文宣受禪，尊為文襄皇后，居靜德宮。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan received the abdication, she was honored as Empress of Wenxiang and dwelt in Jingde Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yang received the abdication, she was honored as Empress of Wenxiang and dwelt in Jingde Palace.

sentences.zh: 及天保六年，文宣漸致昏狂，乃移居于高陽之宅，而取其府庫，曰：「吾兄昔奸我婦，我今須報。

translations.literal: By the sixth year of Tianbao, Wenxuan gradually fell into madness; he then moved her to a residence at Gaoyang and took her storehouses, saying: "My elder brother once violated my wife — now I must repay him.
translations.idiomatic: By the sixth year of Tianbao, Gao Yang gradually fell into madness; he then moved her to a residence at Gaoyang and seized her storehouses, saying, "My elder brother once violated my wife — now I must repay him.

sentences.zh: 」乃淫於后。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he violated the empress.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he violated the empress.

sentences.zh: 其高氏女婦無親疏，皆使左右亂交之於前。

translations.literal: Every woman of the Gao clan, close or distant in kinship, he had those beside him violate in turn before her.
translations.idiomatic: Every woman of the Gao clan, close or distant in kinship, he had those beside him violate in turn before her.

sentences.zh: 以葛為絙，令魏安德主騎上，使人推引之，又命胡人苦辱之。

translations.literal: He made a rope of hemp and had Princess Andrade of Wei mount it, with men pushing and pulling her; he also ordered barbarians to humiliate her cruelly.
translations.idiomatic: He made a rope of hemp and had Princess Andrade of Wei mount it, with men pushing and pulling her; he also ordered barbarians to humiliate her cruelly.

sentences.zh: 帝又自呈露，以示群下。

translations.literal: The emperor also exposed himself and showed himself to the assembled officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also exposed himself and displayed his nakedness before the assembled officials.

sentences.zh: 武平中，后崩，祔葬義平陵。

translations.literal: In the Wuping era the empress died and was given joint burial at Yiping Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuping era the empress died and was given joint burial at Yiping Tomb.

sentences.zh: 文宣李后

translations.literal: Empress Li of Wenxuan
translations.idiomatic: Empress Li of Wenxuan

sentences.zh: 文宣皇后李氏，諱祖娥，趙郡李希宗女也。

translations.literal: Empress Li of Wenxuan, taboo name Zu'e, was the daughter of Li Xizong of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Li of Wenxuan, whose personal name was Zu'e, was the daughter of Li Xizong of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 容德甚美。

translations.literal: Her bearing and virtue were exceedingly beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Her bearing and virtue were exceedingly beautiful.

sentences.zh: 初為太原公夫人。

translations.literal: At first she was Lady of the Duke of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At first she was Lady of the Duke of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 及帝將建中宮，高隆之、高德正言漢婦人不可為天下母，宜更擇美配。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to establish the central palace, Gao Longzhi and Gao Dezheng said a Han woman could not be mother to the realm and that a more beautiful match should be chosen.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to establish the central palace, Gao Longzhi and Gao Dezheng said a Han woman could not be mother to the realm and that a more beautiful match should be chosen.

sentences.zh: 楊愔固請依漢、魏故事，不改元妃。

translations.literal: Yang Yin firmly requested following the Han and Wei precedents and not changing the original consort.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin firmly requested following the Han and Wei precedents and not changing the original consort.

sentences.zh: 而德正猶固請廢后而立段昭儀，欲以結勳貴之援，帝竟不從而立后焉。

translations.literal: Yet Dezheng still firmly asked to depose the empress and install Lady Duan as Honored Consort, wishing thereby to win the support of meritorious nobles; the emperor in the end did not follow him and established the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Dezheng still firmly asked to depose the empress and install Lady Duan as Honored Consort, wishing thereby to win the support of meritorious nobles; the emperor in the end did not follow him and established the empress.

sentences.zh: 帝好捶撻嬪御，乃至有殺戮者，唯後后蒙禮敬。

translations.literal: The emperor loved to beat and flog the palace women, even to the point of killing some; only toward Empress Li did he show ritual respect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved to beat and flog the palace women, even to the point of killing some; only toward Empress Li did he show ritual respect.

sentences.zh: 天保十年，改為可賀敦皇后。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianbao she was renamed Khedun Empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tianbao she was renamed Khedun Empress.

sentences.zh: 孝昭即位，降居昭信宮，號昭信皇后。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao succeeded, she was reduced to Zhaoxin Palace and styled Empress of Zhaoxin.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yan succeeded, she was reduced to Zhaoxin Palace and styled Empress of Zhaoxin.

sentences.zh: 武成踐祚，逼后淫亂，云：「若不許，我當殺爾兒。

translations.literal: When Wucheng took the throne, he forced the empress into illicit relations, saying: "If you do not consent, I shall kill your son.
translations.idiomatic: When Wucheng took the throne, he forced the empress into illicit relations, saying, "If you do not consent, I shall kill your son.

sentences.zh: 」后懼，從之。

translations.literal: " The empress, in fear, complied.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress, in fear, complied.

sentences.zh: 後有娠，太原王紹德至閣，不得見，慍曰：「兒豈不知耶，姊姊腹大，故不見兒。

translations.literal: Later she became pregnant; Prince Shao of Taiyuan came to her gate but could not see her, and angrily said: "Does the boy not know? My elder sister's belly is great — that is why she will not see the boy.
translations.idiomatic: Later she became pregnant; Prince Shao of Taiyuan came to her gate but could not see her, and angrily said, "Does the boy not know? My elder sister's belly is great — that is why she will not see the boy.

sentences.zh: 」後聞之，大慚，由是生女不舉。

translations.literal: " When the empress heard it, she was deeply ashamed; from this she bore daughters and did not rear them.
translations.idiomatic: " When the empress heard it, she was deeply ashamed; from this she bore daughters and did not rear them.

sentences.zh: 帝橫刀詬曰：「爾殺我女，我何不殺爾兒！

translations.literal: The emperor drew his blade and cursed, saying: "You killed my daughter — why should I not kill your son!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drew his blade and cursed, saying, "You killed my daughter — why should I not kill your son!

sentences.zh: 」對后前築殺紹德。

translations.literal: " Before the empress he beat Shao to death.
translations.idiomatic: " Before the empress he beat Shao to death.

sentences.zh: 后大哭，帝愈怒，裸后亂撾撻之，號天不已。

translations.literal: The empress wept greatly; the emperor grew angrier still, stripped her naked, and beat her at random; she cried to heaven without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The empress wept greatly; the emperor grew angrier still, stripped her naked, and beat her at random; she cried to heaven without cease.

sentences.zh: 盛以絹囊，流血淋漉，投諸渠水，良久乃蘇，犢車載送妙勝尼寺。

translations.literal: She was placed in a silk sack; blood dripped and soaked through; she was cast into the canal water; only after a long while did she revive, and an ox-cart carried her to Miaosheng Nunnery.
translations.idiomatic: She was placed in a silk sack; blood dripped and soaked through; she was cast into the canal water; only after a long while did she revive, and an ox-cart carried her to Miaosheng Nunnery.

sentences.zh: 后性愛佛法，因此為尼。

translations.literal: The empress by nature loved the Buddhist Law; on this account she became a nun.
translations.idiomatic: The empress by nature loved the Buddhist Law; on this account she became a nun.

sentences.zh: 齊亡入關。

translations.literal: When Qi fell she entered the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell she entered the Pass.

sentences.zh: 隋時得還趙郡。

translations.literal: In the Sui era she was able to return to Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sui era she was able to return to Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 孝昭元后

translations.literal: Empress Yuan of Xiaozhao
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yuan of Xiaozhao

sentences.zh: 武成胡后

translations.literal: Empress Hu of Wucheng
translations.idiomatic: Empress Hu of Wucheng

sentences.zh: 武成皇后胡氏，安定胡延之女。

translations.literal: Empress Hu of Wucheng was the daughter of Hu Yan of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Hu of Wucheng was the daughter of Hu Yan of Anding.

sentences.zh: 其母范陽盧道約女，初懷孕，有胡僧詣門曰：「此宅瓠蘆中有月」，既而生后。

translations.literal: Her mother was a daughter of Lu Daoyue of Fanyang; when she first conceived, a barbarian monk came to the gate and said: "In this house's gourd-reeds there is a moon"; thereupon the empress was born.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother was a daughter of Lu Daoyue of Fanyang; when she first conceived, a barbarian monk came to the gate and said, "In this house's gourd-reeds there is a moon"; thereupon the empress was born.

sentences.zh: 天保初，選為長廣王妃。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao she was selected as Princess Consort of Changguang.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianbao era she was selected as Princess Consort of Changguang.

sentences.zh: 產後主日，號鳴於產帳上。

translations.literal: On the day she bore the Last Emperor, a bird cried above the birthing pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: On the day she bore the Last Emperor, a bird cried above the birthing pavilion.

sentences.zh: 武成崩，尊為皇太后，陸媼及和士開密謀殺趙郡王叡，出婁定遠、高文遙為刺史。

translations.literal: When Wucheng died she was honored as Empress Dowager; Nurse Lu and He Shikai secretly plotted to kill Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery and sent out Lou Dingyuan and Gao Wenyao as governors.
translations.idiomatic: When Wucheng died she was honored as Empress Dowager; Nurse Lu and He Shikai secretly plotted to kill Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery and sent out Lou Dingyuan and Gao Wenyao as governors.

sentences.zh: 和、陸諂事太后，無所不至。

translations.literal: He and Lu fawned upon the empress dowager to every extreme.
translations.idiomatic: He and Lu fawned upon the empress dowager to every extreme.

sentences.zh: 初武成時，後與諸閹人褻狎。

translations.literal: In Wucheng's time the empress had been familiar with the eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng's time the empress had been familiar with the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 武成寵倖和士開，每與后握槊，因此與后姦通。

translations.literal: Wucheng favored He Shikai; he often played polo with the empress, and through this came to commit adultery with her.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng favored He Shikai; he often played polo with the empress, and through this came to commit adultery with her.

sentences.zh: 自武成崩後，數出詣佛寺，又與沙門曇獻通。

translations.literal: After Wucheng's death she often went out to Buddhist temples, and again had relations with the monk Tanxian.
translations.idiomatic: After Wucheng's death she often went out to Buddhist temples, and again had relations with the monk Tanxian.

sentences.zh: 布金錢於獻席下，又挂寶裝胡床於獻屋壁，武成平生之所御也。

translations.literal: She spread gold coins beneath Tanxian's mat and hung upon the wall of Tanxian's room a precious decorated barbarian couch that Wucheng had used in life.
translations.idiomatic: She spread gold coins beneath Tanxian's mat and hung upon the wall of Tanxian's room a precious decorated barbarian couch that Wucheng had used in life.

sentences.zh: 乃置百僧於內殿，托以聽講，日夜與曇獻寢處。

translations.literal: She then placed a hundred monks in the inner hall, using the pretext of listening to lectures, and day and night shared Tanxian's bed.
translations.idiomatic: She then placed a hundred monks in the inner hall, using the pretext of listening to lectures, and day and night shared Tanxian's bed.

sentences.zh: 以獻為昭玄統。

translations.literal: She made Tanxian Director of Buddhist Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: She made Tanxian Director of Buddhist Affairs.

sentences.zh: 僧徒遙指太后以弄曇獻，乃至謂之為太上者。

translations.literal: Monks from afar pointed at the empress dowager while jesting with Tanxian, even calling her the Grand Sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Monks from afar pointed at the empress dowager while jesting with Tanxian, even calling her the Grand Sovereign.

sentences.zh: 帝聞太后不謹而未之信，後朝太后，見二少尼，悅而召之，乃男子也，於是曇獻事亦發，皆伏法，並殺元、山、王三郡君，皆太后之所昵也。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that the empress dowager was unrestrained but did not yet believe it; later, attending upon the empress dowager at court, he saw two young nuns, was pleased and summoned them — they were men; thereupon Tanxian's affair also came to light; all were executed by law, and the three Ladies of Yuan, Shan, and Wang were also killed — all were favorites of the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard that the empress dowager was unrestrained but did not yet believe it; later, attending upon the empress dowager at court, he saw two young nuns, was pleased and summoned them — they were men; thereupon Tanxian's affair also came to light; all were executed by law, and the three Ladies of Yuan, Shan, and Wang were also killed — all were favorites of the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 帝自晉陽奉太后還鄴，至紫陌，卒遇大風。

translations.literal: The emperor himself escorted the empress dowager from Jinyang back to Ye; at Zimo they suddenly encountered a great wind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself escorted the empress dowager from Jinyang back to Ye; at Zimo they suddenly encountered a great wind.

sentences.zh: 舍人魏僧伽明風角，奏言即時當有暴逆事。

translations.literal: Attendant Wei Sengqie understood wind augury and memorialized that an act of violent treason was about to occur at once.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Wei Sengqie, skilled in wind augury, reported that treason was imminent.

sentences.zh: 帝詐云鄴中有急，彎弓緾槊，馳入南城，令鄧長顒幽太后北宮，仍有敕內外諸親一不得與太后相見。

translations.literal: The emperor pretended there was an emergency in Ye, strung his bow and wrapped his spear-shaft, galloped into the southern city, ordered Deng Changyang to confine the Empress Dowager in the Northern Palace, and issued an edict that none of the inner or outer kin might see the Empress Dowager on any account.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feigned an emergency in Ye, strung his bow and wrapped his spear, galloped into the southern city, and ordered Deng Changyang to confine the Empress Dowager in the Northern Palace, with an edict forbidding all kin, near or distant, from seeing her.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝復迎太后。

translations.literal: After some time, the emperor welcomed the Empress Dowager back.
translations.idiomatic: After some time the emperor welcomed the Empress Dowager back.

sentences.zh: 太后初聞使者至，大驚，慮有不測。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager first heard that an envoy had arrived, she was greatly alarmed, fearing something unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager first heard that an envoy had come, she was terrified, fearing the worst.

sentences.zh: 每太后設食，帝亦不敢嘗。

translations.literal: Whenever the Empress Dowager set out food, the emperor would not dare to taste it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Empress Dowager set out a meal, the emperor dared not taste it.

sentences.zh: 周使元偉來聘，作《述行賦》，敘鄭莊公克段而遷姜氏，文雖不工，當時深以為愧。

translations.literal: An envoy from Zhou, Yuan Wei, came on a diplomatic mission and composed the "Rhapsody on a Journey," recounting Duke Zhuang of Zheng's suppression of Duan and removal of Lady Jiang; though the writing was not polished, people at the time felt deeply shamed by it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wei, an envoy from Zhou, came on a diplomatic visit and composed the "Rhapsody on a Journey," recounting how Duke Zhuang of Zheng crushed his brother Duan and banished their mother Lady Jiang; though the prose was crude, the court felt deeply shamed.

sentences.zh: 齊亡入周，恣行姦穢。

translations.literal: When Qi fell, she entered Zhou and gave free rein to lewd conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell she entered Zhou and gave herself over to debauchery.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中殂。

translations.literal: She died during the Kaihuang era of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: She died during the Kaihuang era of Sui.

sentences.zh: 後主斛律后

translations.literal: Houzhu, Empress Hulu
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu, Empress Hulu

sentences.zh: 後主皇后斛律氏，左丞相光之女也。

translations.literal: Empress Hulu of Houzhu, née Hulu, was the daughter of Left Chancellor Hulu Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Hulu of Houzhu, née Hulu, was the daughter of Left Chancellor Hulu Guang.

sentences.zh: 初為皇太子妃。

translations.literal: At first she was the crown prince's consort.
translations.idiomatic: At first she was the crown prince's consort.

sentences.zh: 後主受禪，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When Houzhu accepted the abdication, she was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Houzhu accepted the abdication, she was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 武平三年正月生女，帝欲悅光，詐稱生男，為之大赦。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Wuping she gave birth to a girl; the emperor, wishing to please Guang, falsely claimed a boy had been born and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of the Wuping era she bore a girl; the emperor, wishing to please Guang, falsely announced a boy and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 光誅，后廢在別宮，後令為尼。

translations.literal: When Guang was executed, the empress was deposed and kept in a separate palace; afterward she was ordered to become a nun.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang was executed the empress was deposed to a separate palace, and afterward was ordered to take the tonsure.

sentences.zh: 齊滅，嫁為開府元仁妻。

translations.literal: When Qi was destroyed, she remarried as the wife of Kaifu Yuan Ren.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell she remarried as the wife of Kaifu Yuan Ren.

sentences.zh: 後主胡后

translations.literal: Houzhu, Empress Hu
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu, Empress Hu

sentences.zh: 後主皇后胡氏，隴東王長仁女也。

translations.literal: Empress Hu of Houzhu was the daughter of Prince Longdong Changren.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Hu of Houzhu was the daughter of Prince Longdong Changren.

sentences.zh: 胡太后失母儀之道，深以為愧，欲求悅後主，故飾后於宮中，令帝見之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager Hu, having failed in the way of a mother to the realm, felt deep shame and wished to please Houzhu; she therefore dressed the empress in the palace and had the emperor see her.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Hu, ashamed at having failed as mother to the realm, wished to please Houzhu; she had the girl dressed and presented in the palace for the emperor to see.

sentences.zh: 帝果悅，立為弘德夫人，進左昭儀，大被寵愛。

translations.literal: The emperor was indeed pleased, established her as Lady of Hongde, promoted her to Senior Lady of Brilliant Beauty, and greatly favored her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, made her Lady of Hongde, promoted her to senior lady of brilliant beauty, and greatly favored her.

sentences.zh: 斛律后廢，陸媼欲以穆夫人代之，太后不許。

translations.literal: When Empress Hulu was deposed, Lu Aun wished to replace her with Lady Mu, but the Empress Dowager would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Hulu was deposed, Lu Aun wished to install Lady Mu in her place, but the Empress Dowager refused.

sentences.zh: 祖孝徵請立胡昭儀，遂登為皇后。

translations.literal: Zu Xiaozheng petitioned to install Lady Hu of Brilliant Beauty as empress, and she was thereupon elevated to empress.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Xiaozheng petitioned to make Lady Hu empress, and she was thereupon elevated.

sentences.zh: 陸媼既非勸立，又意在穆夫人，其後於太后前作色而言曰：「何物親侄女，作如此語言！

translations.literal: Lu Aun, who had not supported her elevation and had her heart set on Lady Mu, later appeared displeased before the Empress Dowager and said, "What sort of mere niece by blood speaks words like these!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Aun, who had not supported the elevation and still favored Lady Mu, later appeared before the Empress Dowager with a dark look and said, "What sort of niece is this, to speak such words!

sentences.zh: 」太后問有何言，曰：「不可道。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager asked what had been said. She replied, "It cannot be spoken.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager asked what had been said. Lu replied, "It cannot be spoken.

sentences.zh: 」固問之，乃曰：「語大家云，太后行多非法，不可以訓。

translations.literal: Pressed to answer, she finally said, "She told His Majesty that the Empress Dowager's conduct is largely unlawful and cannot serve as an example.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed again, she finally said, "She told His Majesty that the Empress Dowager's conduct is mostly unlawful and cannot serve as an example.

sentences.zh: 」太后大怒，喚後出，立剃其髮，送令還家。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager flew into a rage, summoned the empress forth, had her hair shorn on the spot, and sent her back to her family home.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager flew into a rage, summoned the empress, had her head shaved on the spot, and sent her home.

sentences.zh: 帝思之，每致物以通意。

translations.literal: The emperor missed her and repeatedly sent gifts to convey his feelings.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor missed her and repeatedly sent gifts to convey his regard.

sentences.zh: 後與斛律廢后俱召入內，數日而鄴不守。

translations.literal: Later both she and the deposed Empress Hulu were summoned back within the palace; within days Ye could no longer be held.
translations.idiomatic: Later both she and the deposed Empress Hulu were summoned back into the palace; within days Ye fell.

sentences.zh: 後亦改嫁。

translations.literal: She too remarried afterward.
translations.idiomatic: She too remarried afterward.

sentences.zh: 後主穆后

translations.literal: Houzhu, Empress Mu
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu, Empress Mu

sentences.zh: 後主皇后穆氏，名邪利，本斛律後從婢也。

translations.literal: Empress Mu of Houzhu, named Yeli, had originally been an attendant of Empress Hulu's household.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Mu of Houzhu, named Yeli, had originally been an attendant in Empress Hulu's household.

sentences.zh: 母名輕霄，本穆子倫婢也，轉入侍中宋欽道家，姦私而生后，莫知氏族，或云后即欽道女子也。

translations.literal: Her mother Qingxiao had been a maid to Muzilun, then entered the household of Attendant-in-Ordinary Song Qindao, where an illicit affair produced the future empress; her lineage was unknown, though some said the empress was Song Qindao's own daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Qingxiao had been a maid to Muzilun, then entered the household of Attendant-in-Ordinary Song Qindao, where an illicit affair produced the future empress; her lineage was unknown, though some said she was Song Qindao's own daughter.

sentences.zh: 小字黃花，後字舍利。

translations.literal: She was called Huanghua as a pet name and later styled Sheli.
translations.idiomatic: Her pet name was Huanghua; later she was styled Sheli.

sentences.zh: 欽道婦妬，黥輕霄面為「宋 」字。

translations.literal: Song Qindao's wife, jealous, branded Qingxiao's face with the character "Song."
translations.idiomatic: Song Qindao's wife, in jealousy, branded Qingxiao's face with the character for Song.

sentences.zh: 欽道伏誅，黃花因此入宮，有幸於後主，宮內稱為舍利太監。

translations.literal: After Song was executed, Huanghua entered the palace through that connection, won the Last Emperor's favor, and was known within the inner quarters as Director Sheli.
translations.idiomatic: After Song was executed, Huanghua entered the palace by that connection, won Houzhu's favor, and was known within the inner quarters as Director Sheli.

sentences.zh: 女侍中陸太姬知其寵，養以為女，薦為弘德夫人。

translations.literal: Lady Attendant Lu Taiji, aware of her favor, adopted her as a daughter and recommended her as Lady of Hongde.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Attendant Lu Taiji, knowing of her favor, adopted her as a daughter and recommended her as Lady of Hongde.

sentences.zh: 武平元年六月，生皇子恒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Wuping she gave birth to the prince Heng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first year of the Wuping era she bore Prince Heng.

sentences.zh: 於時後主未有儲嗣，陸陰結待，以監撫之任不可無主，時皇后斛律氏，丞相光之女也，慮其懷恨，先令母養之，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: The emperor still had no heir; Lu maneuvered privately, arguing that the role of regent for the heir could not remain vacant—the reigning empress, Guang's daughter, might resent this—so she had the child raised by the empress and established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still had no heir; Lu maneuvered in secret, arguing that the regency could not stand empty—the reigning empress, Guang's daughter, might resent it—so she had the child raised by the empress and established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 陸以國姓之重，穆、陸相對，又奏賜姓穆氏。

translations.literal: Lu cited the weight of the dynastic surname: Mu paired with Lu, and petitioned that she be granted the surname Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu cited the weight of the dynastic surname—Mu paired with Lu—and petitioned that she be granted the surname Mu.

sentences.zh: 胡庶人之廢也，陸有助焉，胡遂立為皇后，大赦。

translations.literal: When the deposed Lady Hu was removed, Lu had helped; Hu was then raised to empress and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Hu was deposed, Lu had helped; Hu was then raised to empress and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 初，有折衝將軍元正烈於鄴城東水中得璽以獻，文曰「天王后璽」，蓋石氏所作。

translations.literal: Earlier, Breakthrough General Yuan Zhenglie had retrieved a seal from the waters east of Ye bearing the inscription "Seal of the Heaven-King's Consort"—a Shi-clan artifact.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Breakthrough General Yuan Zhenglie had retrieved a seal from the waters east of Ye inscribed "Seal of the Heaven-King's Consort"—said to be a relic of the Shi clan.

sentences.zh: 詔書頒告，以為穆后之瑞焉。

translations.literal: An edict proclaimed this far and wide as an auspicious portent for Empress Mu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict proclaimed the find far and wide as an auspicious portent for Empress Mu.

sentences.zh: 武成時，為胡后造真珠裙袴，所費不可稱計，被火所燒。

translations.literal: Under Wucheng a pearl-embroidered skirt and trousers had been made for Empress Hu at immeasurable cost; fire consumed them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wucheng a pearl-embroidered skirt and trousers had been made for Empress Hu at immeasurable cost, only to be consumed by fire.

sentences.zh: 後主既立穆皇后，復為營之。

translations.literal: After Houzhu installed Empress Mu, such garments were commissioned again.
translations.idiomatic: After Houzhu installed Empress Mu, such garments were commissioned again.

sentences.zh: 屬周武遭太后喪，詔侍中薛孤、康買等為弔使，又遣商胡齎錦彩三萬疋與使同往，欲市真珠為皇后造七寶車，周人不與交易，然而竟造焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou was mourning his mother, envoys Xue Gu and Kang Mai were sent as condolence missions; merchant envoys carried thirty thousand bolts of brocade to buy pearls for a seven-treasure carriage for the empress—the Zhou people refused trade, yet the carriage was built anyway.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou was in mourning for his mother, envoys Xue Gu and Kang Mai were sent as condolence missions; merchant envoys carried thirty thousand bolts of brocade to buy pearls for a seven-treasure carriage for the empress—the Zhou people refused to trade, yet the carriage was built anyway.

sentences.zh: 先是童謠曰：「黃華勢欲落，清觴滿杯酌。

translations.literal: A children's rhyme had run: "Yellow blossom's vigor will fade; brim the clear cup and pour."
translations.idiomatic: A children's rhyme had run: "Yellow blossom's vigor will fade; brim the clear cup and pour."

sentences.zh: 」言黃花不久也，後主自立穆后以後，昏飲無度，故云清觴滿杯酌。

translations.literal: It meant Huanghua would not last long; after Houzhu made Mu empress, he drank without measure—hence "brim the clear cup and pour."
translations.idiomatic: It meant Huanghua would not endure; after Houzhu made Mu empress, he drank without measure—hence "brim the clear cup and pour."

sentences.zh: 陸息駱提婆詔改姓為穆，陸。

translations.literal: Lu ordered Mu Tipo by edict to change his surname to Mu, Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu ordered Mu Tipo by edict to take the surnames Mu and Lu.

sentences.zh: 太姬，皆以皇后故也。

translations.literal: Taiji—all on account of the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Taiji too—all on account of the empress.

sentences.zh: 后既以陸為母，提婆為家，更不采輕霄。

translations.literal: Having taken Lu as her mother and Tipo as her family, the empress no longer acknowledged Qingxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Having taken Lu as her mother and Tipo as her kin, the empress no longer acknowledged Qingxiao.

sentences.zh: 輕霄後自療面，欲求見，太后、陸媼使禁掌之，竟不得見。

translations.literal: Qingxiao later healed her face and sought to see her daughter; the Empress Dowager and Lu Aun had her imprisoned and she never gained an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxiao later healed her face and sought to see her daughter; the Empress Dowager and Lu Aun had her imprisoned, and she never gained an audience.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972, as the base for collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972).
